guide.summary: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 user tokens for the User API. The requested listing uses the files.metadata.read scope on list_folder and list_folder/continue, with App Folder access limited to the app folder. Each customer connects through OAuth; the developer's own account can use a generated token only for testing. App registration, redirect URIs and scope selection are setup requirements. Review and distribution policy for other customer organizations is not covered by the supplied snapshots.

steps.title: Send the customer to the Dropbox consent page and check the callback
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and PKCE parameters (code_challenge with S256). The customer signs in and approves the app; Dropbox redirects to the registered redirect_uri with a code query parameter. Verify the returned state matches the value sent. Do not construct consent URLs with example values in production.
steps.doneWhen: The customer approves the app and the browser returns to the registered redirect URI with an authorization code and matching state.

evidence.quote: Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user

https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code in the
Include a code_challenge_method and code_challenge in your authorization URL. The code challenge method may be S256 or plain . Using S256 is the recommended approach.

fields: client_id: app key from Developer Console
redirect_uri: registered exact value
code_challenge: base64url SHA256 of code_verifier
state: random value generated by the web app

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for a user access token
steps.detail: Send the authorization code and the PKCE code_verifier to the token endpoint using the grant_type authorization_code constant. Store the returned access token server-side. For background access, add token_access_type=offline during authorization and store the refresh token.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns an access_token and expiry for the customer account, and the token is stored server-side.

evidence.quote: Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls
In your request to the /oauth2/token endpoint, pass the code_verifier with your generated value instead of the client_id .

When using refresh tokens, your call to the /oauth2/token endpoint with the grant_type of authorization_code will return a short-lived access token and a refresh token, which should be securely stored.

fields: code: authorization code from the callback
grant_type: authorization_code
client_id: app key

code_verifier: original PKCE verifier

steps.title: List the App Folder root and read the first page of entries
steps.detail: Call list_folder with an empty path to list the root of the app's App Folder. The response contains entries (each with .tag and name), cursor, and has_more. Expected successful output is HTTP 200 with entries and has_more. Use the access token from the authorization step; do not use the generated test token for customers.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns entries containing folder or file names and has_more is returned; the cursor is retained for continuation. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: user token from token exchange step
path: empty string for App Folder root

steps.title: Continue listing with the returned cursor until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more is true in the previous response, call list_folder/continue with the cursor from that response. Stop when has_more is false. Preserve the same access token. Do not invent a cursor or assume an empty page ends the listing. Shown here as a continuation step. Call list_folder/continue with the cursor returned by the last response. Repeat while has_more is true and stop when has_more is false. Documented pagination: the cursor from list_folder or the prior continue call is the only paging state.
steps.doneWhen: Continuation calls return entries until has_more is false, and every returned page is merged into the complete listing. The final response has has_more set to false and all entries from every page have been collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

details.title: Each customer authorizes the app with a user OAuth 2.0 token used as a Bearer token
details.detail: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 so the app can access a user's data. The flow returns an access token, which is sent as Authorization: Bearer. The list endpoints document a user-issued OAuth token as an authentication option.

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: files.metadata.read: list_folder and list_folder/continue require files.metadata.read. The App Folder option limits this scope to data within the app folder. Continuation uses the cursor until has_more is false. The read-only scope is documented. Downloads, uploads, edits, moves and deletes are not covered.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Create the Dropbox app with App Folder scoped access
In the Developer Console, create a scoped app with App Folder access and register the exact OAuth redirect URI in the OAuth 2 section of Settings. Record the app key (client_id) and app secret (client_secret); the secret is used only by the server-side token exchange.
Fields: client_id: app key from Developer Console, client_secret: app secret from Developer Console, redirect_uri: exact value registered in OAuth 2 Settings

Enable the files.metadata.read scope on the Permissions tab
On the Permissions tab, enable files.metadata.read only and save changes. Do not enable content read/write or sharing scopes, because they are outside the requested read-only metadata listing.
Fields: scope: files.metadata.read

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Generate a short-lived token for the developer's own account only
Done when: A short-lived access token is shown in Settings and is stored only for local testing.

Send the customer to the Dropbox consent page and check the callback
Done when: The customer approves the app and the browser returns to the registered redirect URI with an authorization code and matching state.

Exchange the authorization code for a user access token
Done when: The token endpoint returns an access_token and expiry for the customer account, and the token is stored server-side.

List the App Folder root and read the first page of entries
Done when: HTTP 200 returns entries containing folder or file names and has_more is returned; the cursor is retained for continuation. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Continue listing with the returned cursor until has_more is false
Done when: Continuation calls return entries until has_more is false, and every returned page is merged into the complete listing. The final response has has_more set to false and all entries from every page have been collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Confirm the grant does not allow reads outside the App Folder or writes
Done when: The out-of-App-Folder read is rejected or the grant and request log show only files.metadata.read; no write request was sent.
